title: Granular quant sensitivity lab - scenario sheet
summary: Interactive, granular worksheet to estimate per-workload cost/latency/quality tradeoffs across INT8, FP8, and 4-bit quantization. Designed for product + applied-ml to run quick sensitivity scenarios and capture recommendation rationales.
assumptions: Baseline: baseline model = open-1.3B (fp16); GPU cost = $0.55/hr (amortized per-token model); host overhead = 8ms per request; kv-cache hit reduces token compute by 65%. Quantization speedups approximate: INT8 = 1.25x token throughput, FP8 = 1.4x, 4-bit = 1.9x (range depends on kernel maturity). Quality penalty is workload-dependent; we map expected delta-utility via a heuristic curve (see formulas). All numbers are mock estimates for planning and must be validated with microbenchmarks.
calc_formulas:
Per-token_compute_cost = (GPU_hour_cost / (tokens_per_hour_baseline * speedup_multiplier)) + infra_overhead_per_token
Tokens_per_hour_baseline = 3e6 (example)
Speedup_multiplier = {fp16:1.0, int8:1.25, fp8:1.4, 4bit:1.9}
Latency_estimate(request) = host_overhead + (seq_len * per_token_latency / batch_effect) - kv_cache_saving
Quality_penalty_score = f(delta_ppl, delta_task_metric) -> utility_loss in [0..1] (we use normalized mapping: 5% ppl increase -> 0.12 utility loss for generation tasks as baseline)
Cost_per_successful_response = per_token_cost * expected_response_tokens / (1 - failure_rate_quality_threshold)
scenario_rows: scenario A | customer-chatbot | SLO=100ms | avg_resp_len=40 | kv_cache=80% | baseline_latency=35ms | baseline_cost_per_1k= $2.6
scenario B | summarization-batch | SLO=500ms | avg_resp_len=200 | kv_cache=0% | baseline_latency=220ms | baseline_cost_per_1k= $18.4
scenario C | search-embed | SLO=50ms (per-doc) | avg_resp_len=8 | kv_cache=N/A | baseline_latency=18ms | baseline_cost_per_1k= $1.1
scenario_table:
ASCII table snapshot (quick calc):

| Quant | Speedup | Est latency delta | Est cost per 1k | Est quality loss | Recommendation 
| INT8  | 1.25x   | -8ms             | $2.08            | low (0.03)        | Good for latency-sensitive chat with kv-cache 
| FP8   | 1.4x    | -12ms            | $1.86            | medium (0.06)     | Balanced pick for mixed workloads 
| 4-bit | 1.9x    | -22ms            | $1.37            | high (0.14)       | Use for high-throughput non-critical quality batches

(Notes: cost numbers derived from Per-token_compute_cost using example tokens/hr; latency delta assumes kernel maturity; quality loss is heuristic - run evals.)
recommendations: Heuristic rules we used: 1) If 95th latency SLO < 80ms and kv_cache_hit >= 60% => prefer INT8 or FP8 depending on eval loss. 2) If cost/unit is dominant (>60% of infra budget) and quality tolerance <= 10% -> FP8 preferred. 3) For batch analytics/summarization where per-item quality tolerance is higher, 4-bit may be acceptable if evals show <15% task degradation. 4) Always keep an fp16 fallback model and automated rollout A/B test for first 2 weeks after quant rollout.
microbenchmark-plan: Small-scale runs to validate: (a) microbench kernels: run 1000 requests w/ seq_len=64,128,512 on target GPU and measure tokens/sec across quant modes; (b) quality eval: run 3 prompt-sets per workload and compute delta-ROUGE/BLEU/PPL; (c) latency SLO tail: capture p50/p95/p99; (d) kv-cache interplay: run with 0/50/90% key hits. Schedule: 2 days per model-size per quant-mode. Owner: Ethan.
